SECTION 9 – OTHER INFRACTIONS

159 
Rule 63 – Delaying the Game 
  
  
63A SITUATION 
 The goalkeeper comes way out of his crease (10 feet) to cut down the angle on a 
shot.  The shot is taken, the goalkeeper catches it and immediately drops it in 
front of him onto his stick, as if to play it to a teammate.  He then notices an 
attacking player is bearing down on him and he drops onto the puck, freezing it 
for a stoppage of play.  Should this be a penalty to the goalkeeper for delaying 
the game? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Yes, since the freezing of the puck was not a direct result from making the save, 
he should be penalized for delaying the game.  Rule 63.2 (i) and (vi). 
  
  
63B SITUATION 
 A minor penalty is being signaled by the Referee against Team A #44.  His 
teammate, Team A #16, who is in his defending zone gains possession and 
control of the puck and as the whistle blows for the delayed penalty, he shoots 
the puck which goes over the glass and into the crowd.  How does the Referee 
handle this situation?  Where do you find this in the rule book?  
  
 ANSWER 
 Since the whistle is blown to stop play as soon as Team A gains possession and 
control of the puck, no additional penalty is assessed to Team A#16 for shooting 
the puck over the glass into the crowd.  Rule 15.1, paragraph 2.  NOTE:  A 
penalty may still be imposed to A#16 if, in the opinion of the Referee, he shoots 
the puck over the glass deliberately as a way of disputing the ruling of the official.  
Rule 40.1 and Rule 63.2 (ii). 
  
  
63C SITUATION 
 Under what circumstance would a penalty not be assessed for a shot by the 
defensive player originating in the defensive zone (non-deflected) that clears the 
glass completely and ends up in the Penalty Bench?  Where do you find this in 
the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 When the puck clears the glass at a point in the Penalty Bench where the glass is 
lower than the normal height around the rink, no penalty shall be assessed. Rule 
63.2 (iii). 
  
  
63D SITUATION 
 A delayed penalty is signaled against the attacking team in the attacking zone.  
The defending player shoots the puck over the glass.  Where is the ensuing face-
off?  Where do you find this in the rule book?

160 
Rule 63 – Delaying the Game 
  
  
 ANSWER 
 The ensuing face-off shall be conducted at the nearest face-off spot in the 
defending zone of the team that shot the puck over the glass.  The defending 
team will also be assessed a delay of game penalty.  Rule 85.1; Rule 63.2 (iii). 
  
  
63E SITUATION 
 A defending player from his defending zone flips the puck high in the air and it 
hits the clock.  Is this a penalty for delay of game?  Where do you find this in the 
rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 No.  The rule for shooting the puck out of play from the defending zone refers to 
shooting the puck ‘over the glass’.  Rule 63.2 (iii); Rule 85.1, paragraph 1. 
  
  
63F SITUATION 
 As a Linesperson drops the puck for a face-off in Team A’s defending zone, 
Team A’s center clearly wins the draw and in doing so, causes the puck to go 
directly over the glass and out of play in his defending zone.  What is the ruling 
on this play?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 No penalty as the puck went out of play as the direct result of a face-off.  Rule 
85.1, paragraph 3 and Rule 63.2 (iii). 
  
  
63G SITUATION 
 With 2:03 left in the third period, Team A shoots the puck into Team B’s end 
zone.  While the puck is in the end-zone, a Team B defenseman deliberately 
dislodges his goal from its normal position.  The puck is not touched by any 
player until it’s stopped by the offending team with 1:59 remaining in the third 
period.  The Referee is about to award the Penalty Shot, but Team B claims that 
the net was dislodge at 2:03 and should have resulted in a stoppage of play and 
be called for a minor penalty instead of a Penalty Shot.  What is the Referee’s 
decision?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 A minor penalty shall be imposed on any player who delays the game by 
deliberately dislodging a goal post from its normal position.  The Referee shall 
immediately stop play when the offending team gains control of the puck.  Rule 
63.2 (iv).  The Penalty shot shall be awarded since the minor penalty cannot be 
served in its entirety.  Rule 63.6, paragraph 2.

161 
Rule 63 – Delaying the Game 
  
  
63H SITUATION 
 A delayed minor penalty is signaled against Team A.  The Team A goalkeeper 
leaves his crease and plays the puck in the corner within the restricted area to 
get the stoppage of play.  Is the goalkeeper also assessed a minor penalty for 
playing the puck in the restricted area?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Yes, the goalkeeper shall be assessed a minor penalty for delay of game for 
playing the puck illegally in the restricted area, in addition to the originally 
signaled penalty to Team A.  Rule 27.8 (see also Rule 63.2 (viii)). 
  
  
63J SITUATION 
 Delayed penalty signaled against Team A.  Team B shoots the puck into Team 
A’s end zone and the Team A goalkeeper comes out of his crease to the top of 
the circle and smothers the puck with his glove.  Do you assess the original 
penalty plus an additional delay of game penalty to Team A?  Where do you find 
this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Although this will rarely happen, Rule 63.2 (vi) specifies that a minor penalty shall 
be assessed to a goalkeeper who leaves his crease and covers the puck to stop 
the play.  Therefore, the rule establishes that the goalkeeper cannot legally 
control the puck in this manner and must be penalized for forcing the play to be 
stopped prematurely.  Had he simply controlled the puck with his stick or skates, 
this would cause the whistle to be blown for the originally signaled penalty and 
only that penalty would be assessed.  However, because he kills the play 
illegally, he too must be penalized. 
  
  
63K SITUATION 
 Fans litter the ice with debris following a goal review that does not result in goal 
for the home team.  What steps should be taken by the officials?  Where do you 
find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The Referee shall have announced over the public address system that any 
further occurrences will result in a bench minor penalty being assessed to the 
home Team.  Rule 63.5. 
  
  
63L SITUATION 
 During the play, the fans throw debris onto the ice that interferes with the 
progress of the game.  What should the Referee do?  Where do you find this in 
the rule book?

162 
Rule 63 – Delaying the Game 
  
  
 ANSWER 
 If the debris interferes with the progress of the game, the Referee shall stop play 
and the ensuing face-off shall take place at a face-off spot in the zone nearest to 
the spot where play was stopped.  Rule 63.5. 
  
  
63M SITUATION 
 With under two minutes remaining in the third period, a defending player in his 
defending zone deliberately pushes the net off its moorings.  What is the 
appropriate call?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The appropriate call is the awarding of a Penalty Shot to the attacking team.  
Rule 63.6, paragraph 2. 
  
  
63N SITUATION 
 With 3:00 remaining in the third period, the Referee has signaled a delayed 
penalty against Team B’s #3 for slashing.  Before play is stopped, Team B’s #3 
deliberately displaces his own net. What would the Referee do?  Where do you 
find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Since the penalties to Team B #3 occurred and were assessed in the order 
described above, the minor penalty for deliberately displacing his own net cannot 
be served in its entirety within the regular playing time of the game.  Therefore, 
he would be assessed a minor penalty for slashing and Team A would be 
awarded a Penalty Shot.   Rule 63.6, paragraph 2. 
  
  
63P SITUATION 
 Under what situations would a Penalty Shot be awarded for delay of game in the 
last 2 minutes of the third period, overtime or due to insufficient time for the 
penalty to be fully served?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
  
  
 ANSWER 
 There are two times.  The first is deliberately displacing his own goal post, Rule 
63.6, paragraph 2 and the second is deliberate illegal substitution, Rule 74.4. 
  
  
63Q SITUATION 
 Team A #8 is assessed a minor penalty with 3:00 left in the third period.  With 
2:30 left in the third period, the Referee signals a delayed minor penalty for 
tripping against Team A #18.  Before Team A touches the puck for a whistle, 
another Team A player (A#28) deliberately displaces his own net to avoid a

163 
Rule 63 – Delaying the Game 
  
  
scoring chance by a Team B player. What is assessed on this play by the 
Referee?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 A#18 is assessed a minor penalty for tripping.  The Referee will also award a 
Penalty Shot to Team B because A#28’s penalty could not be entirely served 
within the regular playing time because of other penalties already being 
served/assessed.  Rule 63.6, paragraph 2. 
  
  
63R SITUATION 
 The Referee has signaled a delayed minor penalty to the attacking team.  During 
a scramble in the crease area, the Referee sees a defending player cover the 
puck with his hand and sweep the puck out of the crease.  Does he award a 
Penalty Shot?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Yes, a Penalty Shot is awarded.  Rule 63.6, paragraph 2 and Rule 67.4. 
  
  
63S SITUATION 
 Team A goaltender is out of his goal crease to cut down the angle of a shot. 
Before he has time to get back to defend his goal, Team B is pressing with many 
shots as Team A defenseman #7 is standing in the goal crease blocking shots. 
One of the shots hits him and the puck is in the air, knee high. Team B attackers 
then begin to storm the crease trying to bat the puck in the net.  Before they have 
the chance, Team A #7 then catches the puck, turns to avoid the attackers, drops 
the puck to his stick and shoots it out of his defending zone. Is this a legal play? 
What actions should the Referee take? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Not a legal play. The Referee shall stop play immediately and award a Penalty 
Shot to Team B.   Rule 63.6, paragraph 2 and Rule 67.4. 
  
  
63T SITUATION 
 Team A is attacking on a 2 on 1 when a second Team B player who is back-
checking dives to break up a pass. The diving player misses the puck and slides 
into the goal, accidentally causing it to be displaced. Just after the net is 
displaced the puck crosses the goal line, between the pegs, where the net would 
have been.  Is this a goal?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Yes, this is a goal. Rule 63.7, paragraph 1 states, “In the event that the goal post 
is displaced, either deliberately or accidentally, by a defending player or 
goalkeeper, prior to the puck crossing the goal line between the normal position 
of the goalposts, the Referee may award a goal.

164 
Rule 63 – Delaying the Game 
  
  
63U SITUATION 
 The net is tipped forward by a defending player just as an attacking player is 
about to shoot the puck into the goal.  Does the goal count?  Where do you find 
this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 There are two factors in play here.  If the goal pegs remain in place and the puck 
enters the net, the goal shall count.  If the net is tipped to an extent such that the 
shot puck is unable to enter the net as a result, the Referee may award a goal if, 
in his opinion, the puck would have entered the net had it been in its normal 
position.  Rule 78.4, paragraph 1; Rule 63.7, paragraph 2.  
  
  
63V SITUATION 
 The goaltender is on the ice, but away from his goal crease. A player of the 
opposing team takes possession and control of the puck and shoots it towards 
the open goal. As the puck is about to enter the open goal, a defending player 
knocks the net off its moorings. What is the Referee’s decision? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The Referee shall award a goal to the team that shot the puck towards the open 
goal.  Rule 63.7. 
  
  
63W SITUATION 
 A defending player, skating towards the attacking defenceman, kicks at the puck 
as it goes by him to block the shot or pass.  The puck goes directly off his foot 
and over the glass.  Does the minor penalty for delay of game apply? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Yes 
 
  
63X SITUATION 
 What penalty is assessed to a player for deliberately displacing his own goal 
posts and his minor penalty cannot be served in its entirety within the regular 
playing time of the game or at any time in overtime? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Penalty shot shall be awarded against the offending team.   Rule 63.6, paragraph 
2. 
  
  
63Y SITUATION 
 The net is dislodged accidentally by an attacking player.  The defending team has 
control of the puck and is breaking out of their zone.  Should play be stopped for 
the dislodged net?

165 
Rule 63 – Delaying the Game 
  
  
  
 ANSWER 
 No.  Allow play to continue until the non-offending team loses control of the puck.  
The resulting face-off will take place at a face-off spot in the zone nearest the 
location where the play was stopped, unless it was in the non-offending team’s 
defending zone, and as such the ensuing face-off would be outside the blue line 
at one of the face-off spots in the neutral zone.  Rule 63.4. 
  
  
63Z SITUATION 
 Team Yellow is on a two on one.  As play moves in towards the Team Blue net, 
Yellow #26 saucers a pass to Yellow #23 who is about to shoot the puck in the 
Blue goal.   Blue #4, who was caught out of position, dives to intercept the pass 
but misses and his momentum carries him into the goal post causing the net to 
come completely off its pegs.   State Referees decision if: 
 
a) Yellow #23 fires the puck top shelf but the net was off prior to the release of 
the shot but he was in the act of shooting. 
 
b) Yellow #23 still has the puck on his stick when the out of position Blue #4 
crashes into the net causing the net to come off. 
  
 ANSWER 
 a) You may award a goal to Team Yellow #23 if you deem he had an imminent 
scoring opportunity.  If there is any doubt of whether the puck crossed the goal 
line legally then the officials may use the Video Goal Judge to assist them in 
making the call.  Rule 63.7 Note:  If Blue #4 lips off, then give him an 
unsportsmanlike conduct minor! 
 
b) If you deem the play by Blue #4 accidental (very unlikely) and Yellow #23 did 
not have an imminent scoring opportunity prior to the net being dislodged then 
NO goal, NO penalty shall be the call on the ice.  IF you deem the act by Blue #4 
intentional and Yellow #23 did not have an imminent scoring opportunity, you 
may assess a minor penalty for delay of game, Rule 63.2 (iv) or if this situation 
occurred in the final 2 minutes of the third period or anytime in overtime you 
would award a Penalty Shot to Yellow #23 Rule 63.6. 
  
  
63AA SITUATION 
 With 2:02 remaining in the third period, Team B shoots the puck into Team A’s 
end.  As Team B is entering Team A’s zone, a Team A defenseman deliberately 
dislodges the net.  As Team A gains control of the puck, the play is whistled dead 
and the score clock reads 1:58 remaining in the game.  The Referee signals a 
Penalty Shot.  The Team A Coach is enraged that the infraction took place with 
more than two minutes remaining therefore a minor penalty should be assessed.  
What is the Referee’s decision?  Where do you find this in the rule book?

166 
Rule 63 – Delaying the Game 
  
  
 ANSWER 
 The determining factor is the time on the clock when the penalty is assessed, not 
when the infraction occurred.  Therefore, the Penalty Shot shall be awarded since 
the minor penalty cannot be served in its entirety.  Rule 63.6, paragraph 2. 
  
  
63BB SITUATION 
 Team A player standing with both feet in the neutral zone, reaches back into their 
defending zone with their stick and propels the puck over the glass.  Is this a 
delay of game penalty? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Yes.  The rule states that, “The determining factor shall be the position of the 
puck when it was shot or batted by the offending player. If contact with the puck 
occurs while the puck is inside the defending zone, and subsequently goes out of 
play, the minor penalty shall be assessed.”  In other words, the instant the puck 
leaves the stick or glove determines from which zone the puck was shot or 
batted.  Rule 63.2 (iii). 
  
  
63CC SITUATION 
 A defending player in his defending zone attempts to clear the puck out of his 
zone by shooting it high off the glass.  The puck goes over the glass and out of 
play, but the puck’s trajectory causes it to land in the Players’ Bench.  Is this still 
a minor penalty for delay of game? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Yes, the determining factor when deciding whether a delay of game penalty is to 
be assessed, is where the puck leaves the playing surface.  If you use an 
imaginary plane that continues upwards to the roof from the top of the glass, 
should the puck break that plane as it goes out of play, then a minor penalty is to 
be assessed regardless as to the final resting place of the puck.  When the puck 
is shot directly into the Players’ Bench (where there is no glass), no penalty is to 
be assessed.  Rule 63.2 (iii). 
  
  
63DD SITUATION 
 Team A shoots the puck over the glass and out of play.  The shot leaves the 
player’s stick six inches over his defending blue line.  Where is the ensuing face-
off? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Even though the rule states that the face-off location must be located at the 
nearest spot that gives the team at fault the least territorial advantage, it also 
states that when the stoppage occurs in the neutral zone, the face-off must be 
taken in the neutral zone.  Rule 76.2, paragraph 3 and Rule 85.1, paragraph 1.  
Using common sense, the face-off should be taken at the dot outside the blue

167 
Rule 63 – Delaying the Game 
  
  
line, even though we may be giving the team at fault a 2-3 foot territorial 
advantage.  You won’t find this specific answer in the rule book. 
  
  
63EE SITUATION 
 Team A's net is knocked off its moorings and Team A gains control of the puck 
and heads up ice.  When is the whistle blown in each situation?  
 
a. Team B knocks the net off? 
b. Team A knocks it off? 
c. Team A knocks it off, but the Referee doesn't notice until Team A is 
skating through the neutral zone? 
d. Team A knocks it off, but the Referee doesn't notice until Team A is in 
the attacking zone?  
  
 ANSWER 
 a. When Team A loses control of the puck. 
b. Since Team A gained immediate control of the puck, whistle blown, 
defensive end zone face-off. 
c. Face-off outside their defending blue line. 
d. Face-off in the neutral zone outside the attacking blue line. 
  
  
63FF SITUATION 
 A Black team defending player standing in his own goal crease, catches the puck 
(above the crossbar), turns to avoid opposing players, and then tosses it towards 
the boards behind the net.  Should a penalty shot be awarded? 
  
  
 ANSWER 
 
No.  Since the puck was above the crossbar when caught and thrown, it was not 
considered to be in the crease.  Therefore, only a minor penalty is warranted on 
this play.  Rule 63.6. 
  
  
63GG SITUATION 
 The Red defenceman breaks his stick as he attempts to clear the puck out of his 
defending zone.  He drops the stick, but with opposing players closing in and the 
puck on the ice, he scoops the puck with his glove causing it to sail over the glass 
behind the players’ bench.  What is the call? 
  
 
ANSWER 
 
Minor penalty for delay of game.  This would be considered shooting or batting 
the puck with his hand resulting in the puck leaving the playing surface.  Rule 
63.2 (iii).

168 
Rule 63 – Delaying the Game 
  
  
63HH SITUATION 
 
The Red goalkeeper makes a save with his stick on a shot.  He was in motion 
from one post to the other when he made the save and the puck propelled off his 
stick and over the glass.  Should he be assessed a delay of game penalty? 
  
 
ANSWER 
 
No.  He was simply making a save and did not “shoot” the puck over the glass. 
  
  
63JJ SITUATION 
 A defending player in the defending zone shoots the puck.  As the puck flies 
through the air, the buzzer sounds to end the period.  The puck goes over the 
glass and out of play.  Is the defending player assessed a minor penalty for delay 
of game? 
  
 ANSWER 
 If it is obvious that the puck left the playing surface (over the glass) prior to the 
expiration of time, the penalty is applied.  Otherwise, no penalty. 
  
  
63KK SITUATION 
 A player is on a breakaway and is over his own blue line in the neutral zone.  As 
he enters the attacking zone, the goalkeeper deliberately dislodges the goal.  
What is the call? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Play shall be stopped, and a goal awarded to the non-offending team.  Rule 63.7. 
  
  
63LL SITUATION 
 The defending team accidentally dislodges their goal causing a stoppage of play.  
What transpires next? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The defending team is not permitted to change any players (except to replace a 
goalkeeper who had been substituted for an extra attacker, to replace an injured 
player, or when a penalty has been assessed which affects the on-ice strength of 
either team).  For the ensuing face-off in the defending zone, the attacking team 
will have the choice of which end zone dot the face-off will take place. 
  
  
63MM SITUATION 
 The attacking team shoots the puck into the attacking zone from their own side of 
the center red line.  The goalkeeper freezes the puck which results in a stoppage 
of play.  What transpires next?

169 
Rule 63 – Delaying the Game 
  
  
 ANSWER 
 The defending team is not permitted to change any players (except to replace an 
injured player, or when a penalty has been assessed which affects the on-ice 
strength of either team).  For the ensuing face-off in the defending zone, the 
attacking team will have the choice of which end zone dot the face-off will take 
place. 
  
  
63NN SITUATION 
A defending player in his defending zone kicks the puck causing it to go over the 
glass and out of play.  Does the minor penalty for delay of game apply? 
 
 
 
ANSWER 
Yes. 
  
  
63PP SITUATION 
 A Team A player in their defending zone attempts to clear the puck and it is going 
to go over the glass at the players’ bench.  Using their stick, a teammate sitting 
on the bench knocks the puck out of the air before it can sail into the spectator 
area.  What is the call? 
 
ANSWER 
If the On-Ice Officials determine that the puck would have cleared the glass 
behind the players’ bench, then a minor penalty for delaying the game – puck 
over glass must be assessed.

170 
Rule 64 – Diving / Embellishment 
  
  
64A SITUATION 
 Team A#17 attempts to draw a penalty for high-sticking by snapping his head 
back.  In your judgment, the stick came nowhere close to his face.  You raise your 
arm to assess A#17 a minor penalty under Rule 64.  How should this penalty be 
announced? 
 
 a.  “Team A#17, minor penalty for unsportsmanlike conduct.” 
 b.  “Team A#17, minor penalty for unsportsmanlike conduct – diving.” 
 c.  “Team A#17, minor penalty for diving.” 
 d.  “Team A#17, minor penalty for embellishment.” 
 e.  “Team A#17, minor penalty for diving / embellishment.” 
  
 ANSWER 
 “d”.  This is the most appropriate description of his actions.  This was discussed at 
training camp. 
 
NOTE:  When this rule was created, it was a subsection of “unsportsmanlike 
conduct”.  It has been a rule all on its own for quite a number of years now (2005-
2006).  As such, the words “unsportsmanlike conduct” should no longer be uttered 
when referring to diving and/or embellishment. 
  
  
64B SITUATION 
 Player on a breakaway is hooked from behind but he clearly goes down easy, 
embellishing his fall to ensure a call is made by the official.  If you as the Referee 
believe he embellished the infraction, what action should you take? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The fact that he has embellished his fall should negate the fact that he was 
“denied a reasonable chance to score”.  As such, a minor penalty should be 
assessed for the original hook and a minor penalty for diving assessed to the 
player that embellished the hook.  Rule 55 and Rule 64.

171 
Rule 65 – Equipment 
  
  
65A SITUATION 
 At a stoppage of play, a goalkeeper proceeds to his players’ bench to receive 
some equipment repairs.  Does his backup have to enter the game immediately? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Yes.  The Referee may use his discretion; however, the repairs should not cause 
any undo delay.  If the repairs are going to be lengthy, the Referee may force the 
team to replace their goalkeeper.

Rule 66 – Forfeit of Game 
  
  
66A SITUATION 
 Team A, in protest of the rulings by the officials, vacate the ice surface, retreat to 
their dressing room and refuse to return after being warned by the Referee as 
outlined in Rule 73.  The score at the time was Team A – 3 and Team B – 0.  The 
Commissioner, through the Hockey Operations Department, declares the game a 
forfeit, thereby making Team B the winner.  What score shall be entered into the 
record books? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Team A – 0 
Team B – 1 
 
Rule 66, paragraph 4.

Rule 67 – Handling Puck 
  
  
67A SITUATION 
 Team A #34 in his defending zone directs the puck with his hand to a teammate 
who plays the puck with his stick in the neutral zone, yet both his skates are 
clearly still in the defending zone.  Should the play be stopped for the hand pass?  
Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Yes, the play shall be stopped for the hand pass. The determining factor is the  
location of the puck, in this case, in the neutral zone. Rule 79.2. 
  
  
67B SITUATION 
 The goalkeeper picks up the puck from the ice and throws it with his blocker hand 
right to a teammate positioned near the top of the circle along the boards.  Is this 
deemed a penalty, or do we allow this play to continue?  Where do you find this in 
the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 This is deemed to be a minor penalty to the goalkeeper for handling the puck.  
Rule 67.3 (iii).   
  
  
67C SITUATION 
 The Referee has signaled a delayed minor penalty to the attacking team.  During a 
scramble in the crease area, the Referee sees a defending player cover the puck 
with his hand and sweep the puck out of the crease.  Does he award a Penalty 
Shot?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Yes, a Penalty Shot is awarded.  Rule 63.6, paragraph 2 and Rule 67.4. 
  
  
67D SITUATION 
 Team A goaltender is out of his goal crease to cut down the angle of a shot. 
Before he has time to get back to defend his goal, Team B is pressing with many 
shots as Team A defenseman #7 is standing in the goal crease blocking shots. 
One of the shots hits him and the puck is in the air, knee high. Team B attackers 
then begin to storm the crease trying to bat the puck in the net.  Before they have 
the chance, Team A #7 then catches the puck, turns to avoid the attackers, drops 
the puck to his stick and shoots it out of his defending zone. Is this a legal play? 
What actions should the Referee take? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Not a legal play. The Referee shall stop play immediately and award a Penalty 
Shot to Team B.   Rule 63.6, paragraph 2 and Rule 67.4.

174 
Rule 67 – Handling Puck 
  
  
67E SITUATION 
 A goalkeeper who is about to be pulled for an extra attacker leaves his goalie stick 
on the ice in front of his net. As he is leaving the ice, but before he is legally 
changed for, the puck is shot down and hits the stick preventing it from going in 
the goal. What is the call and where do you find it in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Since he is still on the ice you cannot award a goal only a minor penalty. Rule 67.3 
(v) and Rule 67.5, paragraph 1. 
  
  
67F SITUATION 
 Team A has pulled their goalkeeper for an extra attacker.  The Team A 
defenseman is standing in his crease when a Team B winger shoots the puck at 
the empty net.  The Team A defenseman grabs the puck out of mid-air (around the 
height of his waist) and drops the puck outside the crease.  What is the Referee’s 
decision?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The ruling on the ice will be an Awarded Goal to Team B.  Rule 67.5, paragraph 2. 
  
  
67G SITUATION 
 A goalkeeper, on his way to his Players’ Bench to be substituted for an extra 
attacker, leaves his stick on the ice in front of his net near the hash marks 
between the two face-off circles.  With the goalkeeper now off the ice, the 
opposing team gains control of the puck and shoots it towards the empty net.  
Although the puck does not hit the goalkeeper’s stick lying on the ice and the shot 
puck goes just wide of the empty net, should the Referee stop play and award a 
goal?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 If in the opinion of the Referee, the stick was placed to prevent the puck from 
entering the net, he shall award a goal in this situation, otherwise a minor penalty 
is to be assessed.  Rule 67.5. 
  
  
67H SITUATION 
 Team A is on the power play.  The puck is cleared down the ice and goes all the 
way to the Team A goalkeeper.  There is no pressure being applied by Team B as 
they are in the process of a line change.  The Team A goalkeeper covers the puck 
trying in an obvious attempt to get a stoppage of play.  The Referee blows his 
whistle and he proceeds to assess the goalkeeper a minor penalty for delay of 
game.  The goalkeeper quickly explains to the Referee that he had a pad strap 
untied and wanted to stop play to fix it.  There is a huddle amongst the officials 
and they decide to take the penalty away, with the ensuing face-off in the Team A

175 
Rule 67 – Handling Puck 
  
  
end zone and play resumes with Team A still on the power play.  Was this the 
correct way to handle this situation? 
  
 ANSWER 
 No.  The minor penalty for delay of game should still have been assessed.  The 
goalkeeper’s untied pad strap cannot be our concern.  Rule 67.3 (ii) states, “A 
delay of game penalty shall be assessed to a goalkeeper who deliberately holds 
the puck in any manner which, in the opinion of the Referee, causes an 
unnecessary stoppage of play.” 
  
  
67J SITUATION 
 A defending player is lying in his team’s goal crease.  The puck is outside the 
crease.  The player holds or grabs the puck, pulling in into his body which is inside 
the crease.  What is the proper call? 
  
 ANSWER 
 A minor penalty for delaying the game should be assessed as the puck was 
outside the crease when the infraction was committed. 
  
  
67K SITUATION 
 A defending player is lying outside his team’s goal crease.  He grabs the puck 
which is inside the crease and pulls it out of the crease and into his body.  What is 
the proper call? 
  
 ANSWER 
 A Penalty Shot should be awarded as the puck was inside the crease when the 
infraction was committed.   Note that the player would be permitted to bat the puck 
out of the crease and not be penalized unless he grabs or covers the puck with his 
hand. 
  
  
67L SITUATION 
 Team A has pulled their goalkeeper.  Team B takes a shot at the on the open net 
where a Team A defender is standing in the crease, trying to stop the shot.  The 
shot hits the defending player in the chest and the puck drops to ice at the 
defender’s feet.  He then drops to his knees on top of the puck.  He does not use 
his hands or arms to gather the puck, but the puck is under him when the Referee 
stops the play.  What is the call? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Awarded Goal, Rule 67.5.  It is irrelevant that he does not use his hands or arms 
to cover the puck.

176 
Rule 67 – Handling Puck 
  
  
67M SITUATION 
 During a mad scramble in front of the net a defenseman for Team A is standing in 
the crease behind his goaltender who is down fishing for the puck.  A shot is 
taken, and that defenseman catches the puck with his hand, which was labeled for 
the top corner.  He then throws the puck into the corner.  What is the Referee’s 
decision? 
  
 ANSWER 
 If a defending player, except a goaltender, while play is in progress falls on the 
puck, holds the puck, picks up the puck or gathers the puck into his body or hands 
from the ice in the goal crease area, the play shall be stopped immediately, and a 
Penalty Shot shall be awarded.  Rule 67.4. 
  
  
67N SITUATION 
 A minor penalty is signaled against Team A#6.  Another Team A player (#23) 
places his hand over the puck while it is on the ice to conceal it from or prevent an 
opponent from playing the puck.  Is Team A#23 immediately assessed a minor 
penalty under Rule 67.2 (ii) resulting in 5 on 3 or is this a situation whereby him 
playing the puck results in possession and control calling for the whistle to be 
blown and only the original minor penalty is assessed? 
  
 ANSWER 
 To be consistent with Situation 63B, as soon as Team A#23 gains possession and 
control of the puck, the whistle is blown for the delayed penalty.  No additional 
penalty would be assessed. 
  
  
67P SITUATION 
Goalkeeper is on the ice and a defending player is standing in the defending goal 
crease.  Puck is shot towards the net and deflects up in the air.  This player, 
standing in the goal crease, closes their hand on the puck above the cross bar and 
then throws it behind the net.  Should a penalty shot be awarded? 
 
ANSWER 
No.  This should be a minor penalty for closing his hand on the puck.  The crease 
only extends as high as the crossbar.  Rule 1.7 and Rule 67.2.

177 
Rule 68 – Illegal Substitution 
  
  
68A SITUATION 
 A player receives a coincidental penalty that will not appear on the clock. The 
penalized player is injured and goes to the dressing room. Following the expiration 
of his penalty time but before a stoppage of play following that expiration he 
returns to the bench. Can he participate in the play (change on the fly) or would he 
be considered an ineligible player?   Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 He would have to be considered an ineligible player as he has not been legally 
released from the Penalty Box.  Rule 8.1, paragraph 3; Rule 68.1, paragraph 2; 
Rule 78.5 (iv). 
  
  
68B SITUATION 
 Team A player is on a breakaway with no one between him and the goalkeeper.  A 
Team B player interferes with the Team A player after illegally entering the game.  
What is the appropriate penalty?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The Referee shall impose a Penalty Shot against the side to which the offending 
player belongs.   Rule 68.3 (see also Rule 70.7). 
  
  
68C SITUATION 
 A player on Team A is in the Penalty Box and is accidentally released by the 
penalty timekeeper prior to his time expiring.  His team has control of the puck in 
the attacking zone when a delayed penalty to Team B is signaled by the Referee.  
Prior to the play being stopped for the penalty, Team A scores a goal while he is 
on the ice.  At the stoppage, it is brought to the attention of the Referee that the 
player was released in error.  What does the Referee do?  Where do you find this 
in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The goal shall be disallowed to Team A.  The penalty to Team B shall still be 
assessed.  The player from Team A must return to the Penalty Box to serve his 
unexpired time.  No additional penalty to Team A as he was released due to the 
penalty timekeeper’s error.  Rule 68.5 (see also Rule 78.5 (iv)) and Rule 70.4, 
paragraph 7 (see also Rule 35.1, paragraph 5) and Rule 70.9. 
  
  
68D SITUATION 
 At a stoppage in play Team A # 4 and Team B # 2 are each assessed minor 
penalties for roughing.  Team B # 2 is also assessed a misconduct penalty.  Team 
B places # 12 in to serve B # 2’s minor and the teams play 4 on 4.  During the play 
when the minor penalties are completed Team B # 2 leaves the Penalty Bench 
due to timekeeper error.  While Team B # 2 is on the ice Team B scores a

178 
Rule 68 – Illegal Substitution 
  
  
goal.  Does this goal count? Is Team B # 2 assessed further penalties?  Where do 
you find this in the rule book?  
  
 ANSWER 
 The goal will not count as he is an illegal player.  The player would have to return 
to the Penalty Box and serve out his misconduct penalty, but no further penalties 
should be assessed.  Rule 68.5. 
  
  
68E SITUATION 
 With major penalties to B-2 and A-4 being assessed at 16:00 of the first period for 
fighting, A-4 goes off to his dressing room due to an injury.  He makes his way 
back to the Players’ Bench area, but play has continued on for some time with no 
stoppages and A-4’s coincidental major eventually ends without a whistle.  His 
Coach puts him out on the fly at the 10:30 mark of the first period where his team 
scores a goal while he is on the ice.  The Penalty Timekeeper informs the on-ice 
officials of A-4’s participation.  What is the final decision at the stoppage?  Where 
do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Disallow goal and assess a bench minor penalty.  Player must have waited until a 
stoppage of play before returning.  Rule 68.2, 68.5 and Rule 78.5(iv).

179 
Rule 69 – Interference on the Goalkeeper 
  
  
69A SITUATION 
 Team A player is in the crease screening the goalkeeper, and Team A scores.  
What is the Referee’s decision?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The goal shall be disallowed, and no additional penalty assessed.  Rule 69.1, 
paragraph 3 and Rule 69.3, paragraph 4, see also Table 18, Section 5 – 
Screening Situations, Example D. 
  
  
69B SITUATION 
 A Team A player is standing in front of Team B’s net with one foot in the goal 
crease.   The Team B goalkeeper comes across the crease and initiates contact 
with the attacking player.  As the contact is made, the puck goes in the net.  Is this 
a legal goal?  If any, what penalties are assessed?  Where do you find this in the 
rule book?  
  
 ANSWER 
 No. If a goalkeeper, in the act of establishing his position within the crease, 
initiates contact with an attacking player who is in the goal crease, and this results 
in an impairment of the goalkeeper’s ability to defend his goal, and a goal is 
scored, the goal will be disallowed.   No goal – no penalty.  The attacking player 
must give ground to the goalkeeper to allow him to play his position within the goal 
crease.   Rule 69.3, paragraphs 2 and 3.  See also Table 18, 6 – Crowding the 
Goalkeeper, sections C and D. 
  
  
69C SITUATION 
 Can an attacking player stand in front of the opposing goalkeeper and hold his 
hand/glove or stick directly in front of the goalkeeper’s eyes/face with the obvious 
intent of impairing his ability to see the puck/play? 
  
 ANSWER 
 No.  This shall be treated as unsportsmanlike conduct and penalized with the 
assessment of a minor penalty under Rule 75 if witnessed by the Referee(s). 
  
  
69D SITUATION 
 Team A#33 and Team B#4 are battling in front of Team B’s net, the attacking 
player A#33 knocks B#4 on top of his goaltender just as the puck is shot and goes 
into the goal.  What is the Referee’s decision and what penalties, if any, are 
assessed? 
  
 ANSWER 
 If a defending player has been pushed, shoved, or fouled by an attacking player 
so as to cause the defending player to come into contact with his own goalkeeper, 
such contact shall be deemed contact initiated by the attacking player for

180 
Rule 69 – Interference on the Goalkeeper 
  
  
purposes of this rule, and if necessary, a penalty assessed to the attacking player 
and if a goal is scored it would be disallowed.  Rule 69.1 see also Table 18. 
  
  
69E SITUATION 
 A goalkeeper initiates contact with an attacking player to establish position in the 
crease by using excessive force or acting in a manner which would otherwise 
warrant a penalty, and the attacking player vacates the crease at the time a goal is 
scored.  What is the call on the ice and where do you find it in the rule book?  
What should the announcement be from the Referee? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Rule 69, Table 18, Situation 6C. A minor penalty to the goalkeeper and the goal is 
disallowed.  This is an example where the attacking player has prevented the 
goalkeeper from doing his job by being in the crease.  The announcement should 
be “no goal due to interference with the goalkeeper (plus the announcement of the 
minor penalty to the goalkeeper).” 
  
  
69F SITUATION 
 A goalkeeper initiates contact with an attacking player in the crease to establish 
his position.  The attacking player vacates the crease in time before a goal is 
scored. Is this a legal play? Where do you find this in rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Goal is disallowed, even though the attacking player vacates his position 
immediately, the contact impairs the goalkeeper’s ability to defend his goal.  Rule 
69.3, paragraph 2 and Table 18, Situation C.

181 
Rule 70 – Leaving the Bench 
  
  
70A SITUATION 
 At 9:45 of the second period a fight ensues between a Team A #24 and Team B 
#6.  During this fight Team A #5 leaves the Penalty Box during the altercation, 
although still having 0:45 to serve on his hooking minor.  Team A #5 does not start 
another fight he just skates around the altercation.  When the fight is over what 
penalties are called and what goes on the penalty time clock? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Team A #24 – major penalty for fighting 
Team B #6 – major penalty for fighting 
 
Team B #5 is assessed an additional minor penalty plus a game misconduct.  The 
Coach of Team B must place a replacement player in the Penalty Box to serve the 
remaining 0:45 and the additional minor penalty to #5.  Rule 70.4, paragraph 5. 
 
Team B will play short-handed for 2:45. 
  
  
70B SITUATION 
 A player on Team A is in the Penalty Box and is accidentally released by the 
penalty timekeeper prior to his time expiring.  His team has control of the puck in 
the attacking zone when a delayed penalty to Team B is signaled by the Referee.  
Prior to the play being stopped for the penalty, Team A scores a goal while he is 
on the ice.  At the stoppage, it is brought to the attention of the Referee that the 
player was released in error.  What does the Referee do?  Where do you find this 
in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The goal shall be disallowed to Team A.  The penalty to Team B shall still be 
assessed.  The player from Team A must return to the Penalty Box to serve his 
unexpired time.  No additional penalty to Team A as he was released due to the 
penalty timekeeper’s error.  Rule 68.5 (see also Rule 78.5 (iv)) and Rule 70.4, 
paragraph 7 (see also Rule 35.1, paragraph 5) and Rule 70.9. 
  
  
70C SITUATION 
 At a stoppage of play, a fight ensues between two opposing players.  They are 
assessed major penalties for fighting.  At the first stoppage of play following the 
expiration of their penalties, the players exit the Penalty Bench and immediately 
engage in another fight (neither is deemed to be the instigator).  What penalties 
are they subject to and where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Both players shall be assessed a major penalty for fighting and a game 
misconduct and are subject to a ten (10) game suspension.  Rule 70.4, paragraph 
8 and Rule 70.10.

182 
Rule 70 – Leaving the Bench 
  
  
70D SITUATION  
 During play Team Blue #75 is skating with his head down again while skating with 
the puck.  Team Yellow #15 steps up and plants a shoulder right in the chest of 
Blue #75 causing him crash to the ice.  In doing so he loses his helmet (the hit is 
legal and NO contact with the head was made).  Blue #75 is ready to cry and 
heads to the Players’ Bench and leaves the ice.  Play continues and Blue #75 re-
enters the game but doesn’t have his helmet on.  State Referees/Linespersons 
decision if: 
 
a) the officials see Blue #75 re-enter the game without his helmet. 
b) Team Blue scores a goal before the officials can blow their whistle for Blue #75 
re-entering the game without his helmet. 
  
 
ANSWER 
 
a) Once the on-ice officials see Blue #75 enter the playing surface, play should be 
stopped once his team has gained control of the puck and a minor penalty shall be 
assessed to the offending player.  Rule 9.6, paragraph 3. 
b) If a goal was scored by Team Blue while Blue #75 was on the ice illegally then it 
should be wiped out and a minor penalty assessed.  Rule 9.6, paragraph 3 and 
Rule 70.9.  
  
  
70E SITUATION 
 Players A12 and B6 are involved in a fight and are assessed major penalties.  A12 
goes to the Penalty Box and B6 goes to his dressing room to take care of his 
injuries.  When B6 returns to his Players’ Bench, his major penalty is still in effect.  
Play continues with no whistle and the major penalty he should be serving has 
expired.  His Coach sends him out on a shift.  He completes his shift and changes 
on the fly.  There still has been no whistle.  Team B now scores.  Should this goal 
count? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Technically, B6 should have been in the Penalty Box awaiting a whistle to be 
released following the expiration of his major penalty.  B6 participated in the play 
as an ineligible player when he played a shift.  Since this could only be brought to 
the attention of the on-ice officials at the next stoppage of play (Team B’s goal), 
and since B6 was not on the ice at the time the goal was scored, the goal shall 
count and B6 assessed a minor penalty.  The penalty shall be for leaving the 
Penalty Box early.  Rule 70.4, paragraph 3. 
  
  
70F SITUATION 
 Player A#5 is assessed a minor penalty at 6:00.   He leaves the Penalty Box early 
(his own error) at 4:02 and then play is stopped at 3:00 for a minor to player B#8.   
What do the Referees do?

183 
Rule 70 – Leaving the Bench 
  
  
 ANSWER 
 A#5 would be assessed a minor penalty for leaving the Penalty Box early in 
addition to the two seconds he must serve in his original unexpired minor penalty.  
Since B#8 is also being assessed a minor penalty at this stoppage of play, they 
are deemed coincidental.  Therefore, 0:02 is put up on the penalty clock for A#5 
and Team A would have to put an additional player in the Penalty Box to serve the 
two seconds left in A#5's original minor penalty.

184 
Rule 71 – Premature Substitution 
  
  
71A SITUATION 
 Late in a tied game, Team A elects to pull their goalkeeper for an extra attacker.  
As the goalkeeper begins to skate towards his Players’ Bench, his teammate 
shoots the puck into the Team B zone.  The extra attacker jumps onto the ice 
prematurely (prior to the goalkeeper being within five feet of the Players’ Bench) 
yet Team B is in control of the puck.  What is the call?  Where do you find this in 
the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The whistle shall be delayed until Team A regains control of the puck.  The 
ensuing face-off shall be conducted at center ice (if play was stopped in Team A’s 
attacking side of center ice).  If the play is stopped in their defending half of the 
ice, the face-off shall be conducted at the nearest face-off spot in either the neutral 
or defending zones (whichever is applicable and provides the least territorial 
advantage).  Rule 71.1. 
  
  
71B SITUATION 
 Team A pulls their goalkeeper near the end of the game for an extra attacker.  The 
player that is replacing the goalkeeper enters the game while the goalkeeper is 
beyond 5 feet of the Players’ Bench.  Team B has control of the puck near their 
blue line and attempts a long pass which is received by a Team A player who is on 
their defending side of the red line (the goalkeeper is now off the ice).  The play is 
stopped for a premature substitution of the goalkeeper.  Is there a penalty that 
comes along with this play?   Where does the ensuing face-off take place and 
where is this found in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 There shall be no time penalty.  The ensuing face-off shall take place at the 
nearest face-off spot to where the stoppage of play occurred.  Since the play was 
stopped behind the red line, the face-off does not occur at center ice.  Rule 71.1. 
  
  
71C SITUATION 
 A delayed penalty is signaled against Team A.  Team B substitutes for the 
goalkeeper too early.  Play is stopped by the Linesperson for the premature 
substitution.   Where is the ensuing face-off?  Where do you find this in the rule 
book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The ensuing face-off shall be at one of the end zone face-off spots in Team A’s 
zone since they are the team being penalized.  Premature substitution of the 
goalkeeper is not one of the four exceptions to the face-off rule following a 
penalty.   Team B, however, loses their extra attacker advantage during the 
delayed calling of the penalty.  Rule 71.1 and Rule 76.2, paragraph 4 (see also 
Rule 15.5).

185 
Rule 71 – Premature Substitution 
  
  
71D SITUATION 
 Is it necessary to announce a premature substitution on the goalkeeper?  Where 
do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Yes.  The public address announcer should be instructed to announce, “Play has 
been stopped due to premature substitution for the goalkeeper.”  Rule 71.2. 
  
  
71E SITUATION 
 Team A #3 has just committed an infraction in the attacking zone. The Referee 
signals a delayed minor penalty. Team B then pulls their goalkeeper in favor of an 
extra attacker.  Before Team A can touch the puck, Team B is whistled for a 
premature substitution. Where is the ensuing face-off? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The face-off shall take place at one of Team A’s end zone face-off spots.  Also, 
the Referee shall have announced through the PA announcer “the play has been 
stopped due to premature substitution of the goalkeeper.” Rule 76.2, Paragraph 4; 
Rule 71.1 and 71.2.

186 
Rule 72 – Refusing to Play the Puck 
  
  
72A SITUATION 
 A defending team player attempts to clear the puck out of his defending zone.  
The attacking defenseman, just inside the attacking blue line, knocks the puck out 
of the air with a high-stick and the puck lands just inside the blue line in the 
attacking zone.  Both teams abstain from playing the puck.  Where is the ensuing 
face-off?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The ensuing face-off shall be conducted at the end zone face-off spot in the zone 
in which the puck was in when the whistle was blown.  Since the attacking team 
illegally contacted the puck with a high-stick, the only team that can legally play it 
is the defending team, and they have abstained from playing the puck.  Therefore, 
the face-off stays in the end zone and must go to the nearest face-off spot in that 
zone.  Rule 72.3; Rule 76.2, paragraph 10, Rule 80.1. 
  
  
72B SITUATION 
 Team A is the attacking team and high-sticks the puck.  The defending team, 
Team B, stands back and refuses to play the puck.  Both teams refuse to touch 
the puck.  What is the call?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The Referee shall stop the play and order the resulting face-off at the nearest 
face-off spot in Team B’s defending zone.  Rule 72.3. 
  
  
72C SITUATION 
 A delayed penalty for slashing is signaled against a player on Team A.  The puck 
is loose in the corner in team B’s defending zone and both teams are refusing to 
play the puck.  What is the Referee’s decision?  Where is the ensuing face-off 
location?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The Referee shall stop play and the ensuing face-off shall take place in Team A’s 
defending zone.  Rule 72.5 and Rule 76.2, paragraph 4.  
  
  
72D SITUATION 
 Team A is shorthanded and has just shot the puck down the ice.  Team A24 is 
then signaled for a delayed penalty for slashing.  With the puck behind the Team B 
goal line, the Team B defender and Team A attacker are standing over the puck 
with neither one attempting to play the puck, what does the Referee do? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The Referee will blow the play down as both players have refrained from playing 
the puck.  He will then assess the minor for slashing to A24 and the face-off will be

187 
Rule 72 – Refusing to Play the Puck 
  
  
conducted in Team A’s end zone.  The on-ice strength will be 5 on 3.  Rule 72.5 
and Rule 76.2. 
  
  
72E SITUATION 
 Defending player in his defending zone bats the puck with his hand or with a high 
stick into the neutral zone and players from both teams refuse to play the puck.  
What happens?  Where is the ensuing face-off?  Where is this found in the rule 
book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The Referee shall stop the play and order the resulting face-off at the nearest 
face-off location to where the play was stopped for this violation.  Rule 72.2 and 
72.3.  The rationale is that the team that batted or high-sticked the puck cannot 
play the puck, only the opposing team can, and should they abstain, the whistle is 
blown, and the face-off stays right there. 
  
  
72F SITUATION 
 Defending player in his defending zone bats the puck with his hand or with a high 
stick all the way down the ice.  A potential icing is signaled by the Linesperson.  
Both teams refuse to pursue the puck for the icing.  What happens?  Where is the 
ensuing face-off?  Where is this found in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The Referee shall stop the play when the defending side abstains from playing the 
puck and the resulting face-off shall be at the adjacent face-off spot nearest the 
goal of the team abstaining from playing the puck.  Rule 72.4 and Rule 81.2, 
paragraph 3.  The rationale is that the team that batted or high-sticked the puck 
cannot play it because the face-off would go all the way back into their zone for 
that infraction, and the opposing team can play it but if they abstain (to attempt to 
run time off the clock), the whistle is blown, and the face-off stays right there. 
  
  
72G SITUATION 
A defending player stands over the puck or stands behind the net with the puck 
and does not move.  Opposing team does not forecheck.  What should the 
Referee do? 
 
ANSWER 
It is the obligation of the team in possession to move the puck forward when able.  
If the Referee observes no attempt by the defending team to move the puck 
forward, a verbal warning (during play) should be issued.  If still no compliance, 
the whistle shall be blown, and a face-off conducted at an end zone face-off spot.  
If the player moves around in the zone or passes the puck between himself and a 
teammate, the play shall be allowed to continue even with no forecheck present.

188 
Rule 73 – Refusing to Start Play 
  
  
73A SITUATION 
 An incident at the end of the first period has the Team A Coach upset.  He refuses 
to bring his team back onto the ice to start the second period.  The Referee orders 
the Coach to return his team to the ice.  How much time is the Coach permitted 
and what steps, if any, are taken by the Referee if the team returns to the ice 
within the permitted time frame?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Once the team is instructed to return to the ice and start play, they have five (5) 
minutes to do so or they shall forfeit the game.  Should they return to play within 
this time frame, they are to be assessed a bench minor penalty for delay of game.  
Rule 73.3.

189 
Rule 74 – Too Many Men on the Ice 
  
  
74A SITUATION 
 During the second period, a team makes a line change where the player exiting 
the ice enters the bench in the opposing teams end zone and the player coming 
on to the ice enters in the neutral zone, (in one door and out the other).  Both 
players are on the ice and within 5’ of the Players’ Bench.  If the player entering 
the ice plays the puck is this considered to be too many men on the ice?  Where 
do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Yes, this would constitute too many men on the ice and a bench minor penalty 
would be assessed.  Rule 74. 
  
  
74B SITUATION 
 Can a goalkeeper be changed “on the fly” (i.e. can the goalkeeper on the ice be 
switched with the back-up goalkeeper while play is in progress)? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Rule 74.1 states, “Players and goalkeepers may be changed at any time during 
the play from the Players’ Bench....”  So yes, goalkeepers can be changed on the 
fly.  However, there are three exceptions to this: 
a. If the goalkeeper on the bench comes into the game at a stoppage of play 
to replace the goalkeeper on the ice who has been injured, they cannot 
switch places until the next stoppage of play.  Rule 8.2, paragraph 4. 
b. If the team chooses to replace their goalkeeper to defend against a Penalty 
Shot, the replacement goalkeeper must remain in the game until the next 
stoppage of play.  Rule 24.2, paragraph 7. 
c. In regular season overtime, once the goalkeeper has been removed for an 
extra attacker, he must wait until the next stoppage of play before returning 
to his position.  Any attempt to return to his position prior to the next 
stoppage of play (“on the fly”) shall be deemed to be an illegal substitution 
and a bench minor penalty shall be assessed.  Rule 74.5. 
It should be noted that the reference to goalkeepers’ substitution in Rule 82.1, 
paragraph 7 pertains to changing goalkeepers during a stoppage of play and is not 
applicable for the scenario presented in this question. 
  
  
74C SITUATION 
 Late in the game, Team A pulls their goalkeeper for extra attacker.   Near Team 
A’s bench, the goalkeeper’s substitute has stepped onto the ice while the 
goalkeeper is within the 5-foot limit and the puck is shot down the ice along the 
boards in front of the bench.  The goalkeeper catches the puck and drops it on the 
ice for a teammate before stepping through the door.  What procedure should the 
officials follow?  Where do you find this in the rule book?

190 
Rule 74 – Too Many Men on the Ice 
  
  
 ANSWER 
 The play should be stopped immediately and a bench minor penalty for too many 
men on the ice assessed to Team A.  Rule 74.1, paragraph 3. 
  
  
74D SITUATION 
 Team A makes a legal line change during the play.  A17 comes on the ice and is 
away from the bench into the play.  A21 is going off but not through the gate when 
the puck accidentally strikes him.  Is this a penalty?  Where do you find this in the 
rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 No, this is not a penalty.  Rule 74.1, paragraph 4. 
  
  
74E SITUATION 
 Under what situations would a Penalty Shot be awarded for delay of game in the 
last 2 minutes of the third period, overtime or due to insufficient time for the 
penalty to be fully served?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 There are two times.  The first is deliberately displacing his own goal post, Rule 
63.6, paragraph 2 and the second is deliberate illegal substitution, Rule 74.4. 
  
  
74F SITUATION 
 When can the goalkeeper change on the fly?  Where do you find this rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 A goalkeeper may change on the fly during regular playing time except when he 
was replaced by a substitute due to an injury.  He must wait until the next 
stoppage (Rule 8.2 and 82.1).  However, a goalkeeper cannot change on the fly 
during regular season overtime, otherwise, this shall be deemed an illegal 
substitution and a bench minor penalty shall be assessed for having an ineligible 
player.  Rule 74.5. 
  
  
74G SITUATION 
 Once the goalkeeper has been removed for an extra attacker in regular season 
overtime, can the goalkeeper return to his position during play or must he wait for 
the next stoppage of play?   Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 He must wait for the next stoppage of play before returning to his position.  Rule 
74.5 and Rule 84.2, paragraph 2.

191 
Rule 74 – Too Many Men on the Ice 
  
  
74H SITUATION 
 
Team A has control of the puck in Team B’s end zone.  Team B is short-handed 
by one player and Team A has the goalkeeper pulled for an extra attacker.  The 
Referee raises his arm for a delayed penalty on Team B.  During the delay, a 
player from Team A jumps onto the ice from the Players’ Bench to join the play.  
What penalties should be assessed?  What is the on-ice strength?  Where is the 
ensuing face-off? 
  
 
ANSWER 
 
The delayed penalty to Team B is assessed and a penalty for too many men on 
the ice shall be assessed to Team A.  These are coincidental penalties and the 
face-off will be conducted at the nearest face-off spot in the zone where the play 
was stopped for the coincidental penalties.  The on-ice strength will remain 5 on 4.  
Rule 76.2, paragraph 5; Rule 74.2. 
  
  
74J SITUATION 
 The Referee signals a delayed bench minor penalty to the Red Team for too many 
men on the ice.  During the delay, the sixth skater leaves the ice which leaves 
them with the correct number of five skaters on the ice.   However, as the delayed 
penalty call continues, the Red Team once again puts a sixth skater on the ice.  
This occurs during the second period.  What penalty or penalties are assessed? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Rule 17 and Rule 74 – Two bench minor penalties are assessed to Team Red for 
having too many men on the ice as these are two separate incidents. 
  
  
74K SITUATION 
 The Linesperson witnesses a too many men on the ice violation on Team A.  He 
cannot stop play immediately because Team B has control of the puck.  He 
verbalizes so that the nearest Referee can hear that Team A is guilty of having too 
many men on the ice.  The Team A Coach hears this and asks the Linesperson, 
"Is that us?  Do we have too many men?"  The Linesperson confirms this with the 
Coach.  The Coach elects to send two more players onto the ice knowing that he 
is already being penalized for too many men on the ice.  What, if anything, should 
the officials do in this situation? 
  
 ANSWER 
 If this occurs when there is insufficient playing time remaining (last two minutes), 
or by reason of penalties already imposed, and the too many men on the ice 
bench minor cannot be served in its entirety, or any time in overtime, a Penalty 
Shot shall be awarded against Team A.   
 
At any other time during the game, the bench minor penalty for too many men on 
the ice would be assessed when Team A gains control of the puck and should the 
officials deem that this act by the Coach was showing disrespect for their too

192 
Rule 74 – Too Many Men on the Ice 
  
  
many men on the ice decision, then a bench minor for unsportsmanlike conduct 
may also be assessed.  Rule 74.2, 74.4 and Rule 39.3(i).

Rule 75 – Unsportsmanlike Conduct 
  
  
75A SITUATION 
 A player in frustration after missing on a breakaway, heads to the bench and 
slams his stick over the bench causing it to break in two and the shaft and blade 
flies back into play, interfering with an opposing player breaking through the 
neutral zone, striking him and causing him to lose the puck (or sustains an injury).  
What should the officials do?  Are penalties assessed?  Where do you find this in 
the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 There are a variety of rules that can be considered by the Referees.  Good 
judgment and common sense would have to prevail when evaluating the situation 
and the result.  Some considerations could be: 
 
Rule 53.2 – minor penalty for interference 
Rule 53.7 – Penalty Shot 
Rule 53.8 – Awarded Goal 
Rule 60.3 – double-minor penalty for high-sticking 
Rule 75.2 – minor penalty for unsportsmanlike conduct. 
  
  
75B SITUATION 
 A player is serving a minor penalty for tripping and 30 seconds into his penalty he 
verbally abuses an official from the Penalty Box. He is assessed an additional 
minor penalty for unsportsmanlike conduct.  Does another player have to serve 
this additional minor penalty or does the penalty time get added onto his unexpired 
penalty time?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 If a penalized player is assessed an additional unsportsmanlike conduct penalty 
either before or after he begins serving his original penalty(ies), the additional 
minor penalty is added to his unexpired time and served consecutively.  Rule 75.2, 
paragraph 2 and Rule 39.2(vi). 
  
  
75C SITUATION 
 It was the night before Christmas, Santa’s team was in a funk, not a player was 
working hard, they seemed to be eggnog-drunk.  The Big man behind the bench 
that night had seen enough, and after their 5
th
 consecutive minor penalty, flung a 
water bottle with one huge huff.  It bounces off the ice and slides by the Referee 
who was delivering the bad news, to the thousands of fans and their chorus of 
boos.  This act was witnessed by all the crack crew, so my question to you is, 
what do you do?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 A bench minor for unsportsmanlike conduct would be applied if, in the opinion of 
the Referee, the object was thrown onto the ice with no attempt to direct it towards 
the officials.  Rule 75.3(i); Table 1.

194 
Rule 75 – Unsportsmanlike Conduct 
  
  
A game misconduct would be applied if, in the opinion of the Referee, the object 
was thrown in the general direction of an official but does not come close to 
making any contact.  Rule 39.5(vi). 
  
  
75D SITUATION 
 Can an attacking player stand in front of the opposing goalkeeper and hold his 
hand/glove or stick directly in front of the goalkeeper’s eyes/face with the obvious 
intent of impairing his ability to see the puck/play? 
  
 ANSWER 
 No.  This shall be treated as unsportsmanlike conduct and penalized with the 
assessment of a minor penalty under Rule 75 if witnessed by the Referee(s). 
  
  
75E SITUATION 
 Team A has iced the puck.  The players and officials quickly get into position for 
the ensuing face-off.  A water bottle is seen coming off the Team A bench into the 
neutral zone, but the Linesperson who witnessed the water bottle coming off the 
bench cannot determine who specifically “dropped” (threw) the water bottle.  What 
should the officials do?  Where do you find this in the rule book?   
  
 ANSWER 
 Bench minor penalty for Unsportsmanlike Conduct shall be assessed.  Rules 53.3, 
75.3, 32.4, and they may now change, Rule 81.4. 
  
  
75F SITUATION 
 After a fight, the Team A player makes an obscene gesture to the crowd on the 
way to the Penalty Box.  What penalty is assessed? 
  
 ANSWER 
 A game misconduct penalty is to be assessed.  Rule 75.5 (ii) 
  
  
75G SITUATION 
An On-Ice Official observes a player “lick” an opponent.  What, if anything, should 
be assessed? 
 
ANSWER 
At a minimum, the player guilty of this type of gesture should be assessed a minor 
penalty for Unsportsmanlike Conduct.  Rule 75.2(ii).

195 
Rule 75 – Unsportsmanlike Conduct 
  
  
75H SITUATION 
 A player is told by one of the officials to refrain from hanging his legs over the 
boards waiting for a player change.  Yet he continues to do so.  What, if anything, 
should the officials do? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Any player who continually defies the direction of the Referee and/or Linesperson 
can be assessed an Unsportsmanlike Conduct minor penalty.  If the behavior 
continues, a misconduct or game misconduct could be imposed.  Rule 75.2

Rule 76 – Face-offs 
  
  
76A SITUATION 
 An attacking player in the neutral zone bats the puck with his hand into the 
attacking zone causing a delayed off-side.  His teammate in the attacking zone 
intentionally plays the puck during the delayed off-side.  The whistle is blown for 
two rule violations, the hand pass and the off-side.  Where is the ensuing face-
off?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The ensuing face-off shall be conducted at one of the face-off spots in the 
offending team’s defending zone.  Rule 76.2, paragraph 2. 
  
  
76B SITUATION 
 Team A player is skating with the puck and crosses his own blue line into the 
neutral zone.  The whistle is blown to stop the play as a fight has broken out 
elsewhere on the ice.  Where is the ensuing face-off?  Where do you find this in 
the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The ensuing face-off shall be conducted at the nearest face-off dot outside 
Team A’s blue line.  Rule 76.2, paragraph 3. 
  
  
76C SITUATION 
 An attacking player in the neutral zone attempts a pass to a teammate.  The 
puck is deflected out of play by a defending player in the neutral zone.  It hits his 
stick between the face-off dot and his own defending blue line.  Where is the 
ensuing face-off?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Even though the rule states that the face-off location must be located at the 
nearest spot that gives the team at fault the least territorial advantage, it also 
states that when the stoppage occurs in the neutral zone, the face-off must be 
taken in the neutral zone.  Rule 76.2, paragraph 3 and Rule 85.1, paragraph 1.  
Using common sense, the face-off should be taken at the dot outside the blue 
line, even though we may be giving the team at fault a 2-3 foot territorial 
advantage.  You won’t find this specific answer in the rule book. 
  
  
76D SITUATION 
 Team A #3 has just committed an infraction in the attacking zone. The Referee 
signals a delayed minor penalty. Team B then pulls their goalkeeper in favor of 
an extra attacker.  Before Team A can touch the puck, Team B is whistled for a 
premature substitution. Where is the ensuing face-off?

200 
Rule 76 – Face-offs 
  
  
 ANSWER 
 The face-off shall take place at one of Team A’s end zone face-off spots.  Also, 
the Referee shall have announced through the PA announcer “the play has 
been stopped due to premature substitution of the goalkeeper.” Rule 76.2, 
paragraph 4; Rule 71.1 and 71.2. 
  
  
76E SITUATION 
 On an icing play, the back Linesperson sees the puck deflected by the non-
offending team, however the front Linesperson doesn’t notice the wave off and 
calls icing on the play.  At the completion of the icing play, an attacker finishes 
the defending player into the boards and the Referee signals a minor for 
boarding.  Now the back Linesperson overrules the icing call and the attacker 
pleads his case saying he knew that icing was nullified as he seen the puck 
deflected in neutral ice.  What do the officials do?  Where do you find this in the 
rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The minor penalty for boarding is still assessed.  The ensuing face-off will be 
conducted in the penalized team’s defending zone.  Rule 41.1, paragraph 3; 
Rule 76.2, paragraph 4. 
  
  
76F SITUATION 
 A delayed penalty has been signaled against Team A.  Team B shoots the puck 
into the attacking zone, a delayed off-side is signaled but the puck deflects off a 
Team A player out of play.  Where is the ensuing face-off?  Where do you find 
this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Face-off in Team A’s end zone.  Rule 76.2, paragraph 4 and Rule 83.5 
paragraph 5.   
  
  
76G SITUATION 
 A delayed penalty for slashing is signaled against a player on Team A.  The 
puck is loose in the corner in team B’s defending zone and both teams are 
refusing to play the puck.  What is the Referee’s decision?  Where is the 
ensuing face-off location?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The Referee shall stop play and the ensuing face-off shall take place in Team 
A’s defending zone.  Rule 72.5 and Rule 76.2, paragraph 4.

201 
Rule 76 – Face-offs 
  
  
76H SITUATION 
 Team A ices the puck and the players go back into Team A’s end zone to take 
the face-off.  Before the puck is dropped, a Team B player is assessed a minor 
penalty.  Where does the ensuing face-off take place?  Where do you find it in 
the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The ensuing face-off will take place at one of the face-off spots in Team B’s 
defending zone.  The penalty was incurred after play was stopped for the icing.  
Rule 76.2, paragraph 5  
  
  
76J SITUATION 
 Team A shoots the puck down the ice and it results in an icing being called.  
After the whistle is blown for the icing, Team B#89 turns around and slashes 
Team A#50, resulting in a minor penalty.  Where is the ensuing face-off? 
  
 ANSWER 
 After the play is stopped due to an icing being called against Team A, Team 
B#89 commits an infraction and is assessed a minor penalty.  The ensuing face-
off shall take place in the Team B’s end zone due to the penalty assessment. 
Rule 76.2 paragraph 5 
  
  
76K SITUATION 
 A delayed penalty is signaled against Team A.  Team B substitutes for the 
goalkeeper too early.  Play is stopped by the Linesperson for the premature 
substitution.   Where is the ensuing face-off?  Where do you find this in the rule 
book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The ensuing face-off shall be at one of the end zone face-off spots in Team A’s 
zone since they are the team being penalized.  Premature substitution of the 
goalkeeper is not one of the four exceptions to the face-off rule following a 
penalty.   Team B, however, loses their extra attacker advantage during the 
delayed calling of the penalty.  Rule 71.1 and Rule 76.2, paragraph 4. 
  
  
76L SITUATION 
 With 4:59 remaining in the third period, Team A is assessed a major penalty and 
Team B is assessed a minor. What goes on the clock?  Where is the ensuing 
face-off conducted?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Team A will have 3:00 placed on the penalty clock (major penalty) and Team B 
will have no time placed on the penalty time clock.  The ensuing face-off will be

202 
Rule 76 – Face-offs 
  
  
conducted at one of the end zone face-off spots in Team A’s defending zone.  
Rule 19.4 and Rule 76.2, paragraph 4. 
  
  
76M SITUATION 
 A delayed penalty has been signaled against Team A.   Team B has control of 
the puck in Team A’s end zone and an attempted pass back to the point man 
goes all the way down the ice and icing is called in error by the Linesperson.   
Where is the ensuing face-off?  What rule(s) do you refer to in order to justify 
your answer? 
  
 ANSWER 
 This was not an icing play and therefore cannot be treated as an error in the 
calling of icing.  Since Team A is being penalized, the ensuing face-off must be 
conducted at one of the face-off spots in Team A’s defending zone.  The only 
consequence to the error by the Linesperson was that Team B was denied their 
opportunity to attempt to score with an extra attacker on the ice in place of the 
goalkeeper.  Rule 76.2, paragraph 4. 
  
  
76N SITUATION 
 A delayed penalty is signaled against the attacking team in the attacking zone.  
The defending player shoots the puck over the glass.  Where is the ensuing 
face-off?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The ensuing face-off shall be conducted at the nearest face-off spot in the 
defending zone of the team that shot the puck over the glass.  The defending 
team will also be assessed a delay of game penalty.  Rule 76.2, paragraph 5, 
Rule 85.1, Rule 63.2 (iii). 
  
  
76P SITUATION 
 During the opening face-off, a player is assessed a minor penalty before the 
puck is dropped.  Where is the ensuing face-off?  Where do you find this in the 
rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The face-off would take place at center ice. Rule 76.2 (ii). 
  
  
76Q SITUATION 
 The whistle goes in Team A’s end zone.  A scrum ensues and the defencemen 
from Team B come deep into the zone well below the top of the face-off circles.  
A player from Team A punches one of the defencemen from Team B and is 
assessed the only minor penalty.  Where is the resulting face-off?   Where do 
you find this in the rule book?

203 
Rule 76 – Face-offs 
  
  
 ANSWER 
 As soon as the defencemen from Team B enters the zone beyond the top of the 
face-off circles, the face-off would move to the neutral zone. This is one of the 
four exceptions listed under Rule 76.2 that determines the location of the face-
off following the assessment of a penalty to one team.  (NOTE:  This 
supersedes the direction given in a Face-off memo dated 10/20/2008.) 
  
  
76R SITUATION 
 A defending team player attempts to clear the puck out of his defending zone.  
The attacking defenseman, just inside the attacking blue line, knocks the puck 
out of the air with a high-stick and the puck lands just inside the blue line in the 
attacking zone.  Both teams abstain from playing the puck.  Where is the 
ensuing face-off?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 The ensuing face-off shall be conducted at the end zone face-off spot in the 
zone in which the puck was in when the whistle was blown.  Since the attacking 
team illegally contacted the puck with a high-stick, the only team that can legally 
play it is the defending team, and they have abstained from playing the puck.  
Therefore, the face-off stays in the end zone and must go to the nearest face-off 
spot in that zone.  Rule 72.3; Rule 76.2, paragraph 10, Rule 80.1. 
  
  
76S SITUATION 
 Team A in their attacking zone is called for a minor penalty.  The ensuing face-
off will take place at one of the face-off spots in Team A’s defending zone.  
Before play resumes, a Team B player takes a minor penalty.  Does this change 
the face-off location?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Yes.  The original stoppage of play was to assess a penalty to Team A.  That 
stoppage occurred in Team B’s end zone.  Since both teams are being 
penalized at the same stoppage of play, the face-off must be relocated to the 
nearest face-off spot to where the original stoppage of play occurred (Team B’s 
end zone).  Rule 76.2, paragraph 5. 
  
  
76T SITUATION 
 A player ices the puck from his own defending zone.  On the way down the ice, 
the puck hits an official in the neutral zone and then goes directly into the 
opposing teams’ goal.  This is no goal, however, where is the ensuing face-off 
conducted?  Where do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Although not specifically covered in the rules, the face-off should take place at 
the nearest face-off spot in the neutral zone near to where the puck hit the

204 
Rule 76 – Face-offs 
  
  
official.  This would be consistent with Rule 76.2, paragraph 8 and Rule 85.4, 
paragraph 4 (referring to face-off location when puck strikes official and goes out 
of play). 
  
  
76U SITUATION 
 Team A is in their attacking zone.  The puck comes off the ice and a Team A 
player knocks it out of the air with his stick.  The Referee in the end zone 
washes out the potential high-sticking the puck infraction, but the Referee in the 
neutral zone blows the whistle for the infraction.  Where is the ensuing face-off? 
  
 ANSWER 
 Should this occur, the on-ice officials must confer to make the correct decision.  
If it is decided that a high-sticking the puck infraction did in fact occur, the face-
off must be taken at the face-off spot in the neutral zone outside Team A’s 
attacking.  If it is determined that the play was stopped in error, the face-off must 
be taken at the nearest face-off spot to where the puck was when the whistle 
was blown.  Rule 80.2, Rule 80.4, paragraph 1 and Rule 76.2, paragraph 10. 
  
  
76V SITUATION 
 The Linesperson blows his whistle to start the five-second warning for the 
ensuing face-off in the defending zone.  The defending center is back from the 
dot talking to a defenceman.  The five-seconds ends, and he is not yet at the 
face-off dot.  What is the procedure for the Linesperson at that moment?  Where 
do you find this in the rule book? 
  
 ANSWER 
 If a center is not at the designated face-off area once the five-second time has 
elapsed, the Linesperson will drop the puck immediately.  If the center is back 
from the dot, “quarterbacking” or refuses to come when instructed, or is just slow 
getting there by the time the five-seconds has elapsed, the puck will be dropped.  
If the center tries to time the drop, he will be removed, and it will be considered 
a face-off violation.  Rule 76.4, paragraph 4. 
  
  
76W SITUATION 
 Teams are lined up for an end zone face-off with each team having a player 
positioned behind the Linesperson dropping the puck.  In anticipation of the 
puck being dropped, the attacking player behind the Linesperson jumps into the 
circle 2 to 3 feet, quickly stops and is in the process of backing up when the
